numvault.metaDesc: Can you crack the hidden number code? NumVault is a free number deduction puzzle with daily challenges.
numvault.guide: Crack a hidden code of 4–6 digits using the feedback after each guess. Green means the correct digit in the correct position; yellow means a matching digit belongs elsewhere. Gray means this copy of the digit has no unmatched place in the code. Exact matches are assigned first, which matters when digits repeat. The Number Tracker summarizes clues for digits 0–9, while the guess rows preserve position information. Easy uses four different digits; higher difficulties allow repeats. Daily offers one recorded attempt on the shared UTC puzzle, then Free Play remains available. Speed starts with 60 seconds and adds 15 seconds for each solved code. Try broad guesses first, then use the clues to narrow positions. Hints reveal one position: up to one in Daily or two in Free Play, with none in Speed.
numvault.faq1a: It summarizes the clues for digits 0–9 below the grid. Check the guess rows for each position and repeated-digit counts.
numvault.faq2a: Green matches are assigned first, then yellow matches use remaining copies of each digit. Gray means no unmatched copy remains, so it does not always rule out that digit entirely.
numvault.faq3a: Easy uses distinct digits. Normal, Hard, and Expert allow repeated digits.
numvault.faq4a: At midnight UTC. Everyone gets the same code. After your daily attempt is recorded, use Free Play until the next puzzle.
numvault.faq5a: A hint reveals one unconfirmed position. Daily allows one, Free Play two, and Speed none. Using one removes the no-hint score bonus and is noted in the shared result. Help is currently free; a configured reward ad would ask first.

gridsmash.tagline: Place blocks, clear lines, chase combos
gridsmash.metaDesc: GridSmash is a free block placement puzzle. Clear lines, trigger combos, and use special blocks for massive scores.
gridsmash.guide: Build a clean board one placement at a time. GridSmash gives you three pieces for a 10 by 10 board. Drag a piece from the tray and release it over empty cells. A short tap on a tray piece rotates it; desktop players can also right-click while dragging. Complete all three pieces to receive a fresh set. Green outlines preview the ordinary rows and columns your placement would complete, so you can compare a simple clear with a crossing-line combo before committing.
gridsmash.faq1a: Twenty shapes use one to five cells: dots, lines, corners, squares, and more. Rotate a piece to test different placements.
gridsmash.faq2a: From turn 10 outside Zen, a crystal clears a nearby 3×3 area as soon as you place it and adds 200 points. Frost creates two frozen cells requiring two line-clear hits. A gold wild is a single-cell piece and must be placed on an empty cell. Specials may change neighboring cells, so the green line preview is shown only for ordinary pieces.
gridsmash.faq3a: Every ten turns the bottom two rows become a Shatter Zone for three turns. Completing a row in the zone triples its line score. When the zone expires, three empty cells in the zone fill with blocks if space is available.
gridsmash.faq4a: Placed cells earn 10 points each. Line clears reward simultaneous lines and consecutive clears. Crystals add 200; Shatter Zone rows triple their line points; an empty-board clear adds 5,000.
gridsmash.faq5a: Classic lasts while a remaining piece can fit, including rotations. Daily uses a shared three-minute sequence. Sprint aims for 40 lines. Zen removes special pieces and the Shatter Zone.
gridsmash.guide2: For keyboard play, focus the board and choose a piece with 1, 2, or 3. Move its preview with the arrow keys, rotate with R, and press Enter to place it. Escape cancels the preview. Filled rows and columns clear together. Each placed cell earns 10 points, and completed lines earn points with bonuses for consecutive clearing placements. Leave room for wide pieces and consider rotating before giving up on a tight space.
gridsmash.guide3: Special pieces begin appearing from turn 10 outside Zen mode. Placing a crystal clears a nearby 3 by 3 area and adds 200 points immediately. A frost piece creates two frozen cells that need two line-clear hits. The gold wild is a single-cell piece and still needs an empty cell. Every ten turns the bottom two rows become a three-turn Shatter Zone: completing a row there gives triple line points. When the zone expires, three empty cells may fill. Daily uses a shared seeded sequence and a three-minute timer; Sprint asks you to clear 40 lines. Zen removes special pieces and the Shatter Zone.

patternpop.metaDesc: Test your visual memory with PatternPop. Memorize flashing patterns and tap them back. Beware of decoy flashes!
patternpop.guide: Press Ready, watch the blue ◆ pads, then select their remembered positions after they disappear. Order does not matter. The board grows from 3×3 to 6×6 as rounds advance. From round 5, brief red × decoys appear; ignore them. Use touch or focus the board and move with arrow keys, then Enter or Space to select. Each completed round scores 100 times its target count, doubled for an error-free round averaging under half a second per target. Classic and Daily start with three lives. Daily repeats the shared seeded layouts and can be replayed for practice. Endless has unlimited lives; Speed starts with just one. A hint replays the same pattern at a slower pace without changing the targets.
patternpop.faq1a: Rounds 1–4 use 3×3, 5–8 use 4×4, 9–14 use 5×5, and round 15 onward uses 6×6.
patternpop.faq2a: From round 5, red × pads flash for 0.3 seconds. Only the blue ◆ targets count. Selecting a decoy or another wrong pad costs a life. Decoys increase up to four.
patternpop.faq3a: A completed round earns 100 × target count. No mistakes and an average under 0.5 seconds per target doubles that round’s points.
patternpop.faq4a: The hint replays the current pattern more slowly and keeps targets already found. Help is currently free. If a reward provider is connected, it will ask before showing an ad.
patternpop.faq5a: Classic and Daily start with three lives. Daily uses shared seeded layouts and allows replays. Endless has unlimited lives. Speed starts with one life; its memorization timing currently matches Classic.

sortstack.metaDesc: SortStack is a free color sorting puzzle. Move blocks between stacks to group colors. Can you solve it in minimum moves?
sortstack.guide: Sort the numbered, colored balls into glass tubes containing four matching balls each. Select a tube’s top ball, then a destination with a matching top ball or an empty space. Green rims show legal destinations. A completed tube locks and adds an empty tube for more working room. The ball numbers also identify colors. Scroll sideways to reach more tubes on a narrow screen. Undo is free and unlimited; hints suggest a useful next move rather than proving an optimal solution. Classic offers Easy with unlimited moves, Medium with 50, Hard with 40, and Expert with 35. Relaxed removes move limits. Start by protecting empty tubes so you have space to rearrange mixed colors.
sortstack.faq1a: Four matching balls complete a tube. It locks, and a new empty tube gives you more room to sort.
sortstack.faq2a: Yes. Undo is free and unlimited.
sortstack.faq3a: Easy: 3 colors, 5 tubes, unlimited moves. Medium: 5 colors, 7 tubes, 50 moves. Hard: 7 colors, 9 tubes, 40 moves. Expert: 10 colors, 12 tubes, 35 moves. Relaxed removes limits; Daily selects a difficulty for the day.
sortstack.faq4a: Boards are constructed by scrambling a solved arrangement with reverse moves. This does not prove the shortest solution or guarantee completion within a difficulty’s move limit. Use Undo or Relaxed to explore.

quickcalc.tagline: Race against time with mental math
quickcalc.metaDesc: QuickCalc is a speed math game. Solve problems against the clock. Can you handle the Operator Roulette?
quickcalc.guide: Choose the correct answer, or use keys 1–4. Consecutive correct answers build a combo for more points. Classic and Daily give you 3 hearts and a timer for each question. The daily course changes at midnight UTC and can be replayed for practice. Timed modes subtract 3 seconds for each wrong answer. A 30-second duel uses the same question sequence and answer positions for both friends, with no hints or extra time. Share your result to send that exact course to a friend. Challenge scores are self-reported and are not a verified leaderboard.
quickcalc.faq1a: Classic: three lives and a timer per question. Daily: the shared daily course, replayable. Time Attack: two minutes, with a three-second penalty per wrong answer. Duel: a shared 30-second course without hints or extra time.
quickcalc.faq2a: Correct answers earn 100 × phase, plus remaining seconds ×10 and consecutive correct answers ×50. Operator questions double the answer’s points.
quickcalc.faq3a: From question 11, some questions hide one operator, such as 7 ? 3 = 21. Choose × to solve it. Correct operator answers earn double points. Outside duels, a hint can narrow the choices to two.
quickcalc.faq4a: Numeric choices mix the correct value with nearby and more distant errors, then shuffle their positions. Duel friends receive the same choices in the same positions.

tileturn.tagline: Flip tiles to light them all
tileturn.metaDesc: TileTurn is a tile-flipping puzzle with 3 unique modes: Classic, Cascade, and Spectrum. Solve puzzles with logical thinking.
tileturn.guide: Every tap changes several tiles. In Classic, the selected tile and its up, down, left, and right neighbors toggle ON or OFF; light every tile to finish. Cascade starts the same way, then only first-step tiles that became ON toggle their own neighbors after a short delay. Spectrum cycles dark ○ → blue ◆ → green ✓; the goal is every tile green. Preview the affected area before tapping and use free Undo to compare ideas. Seven packs contain 140 levels. The displayed move target comes from puzzle construction, not a proof of the fewest possible moves. Finish at or below that target for three stars, within two extra moves for two stars, or complete the board for one.
tileturn.faq1q: Is the move target a proven minimum?
tileturn.faq1a: No. Puzzles are constructed backwards from a completed board. The construction length sets the scoring target; a shorter solution may exist.
tileturn.faq2a: Undo restores the previous board and subtracts that move from the counter. It is free.
tileturn.faq3a: All seven packs are available. Within each pack, complete levels in sequence. There are 140 levels in total.
tileturn.faq4a: First, the target and its four neighbors toggle. After 300 ms, only those that became ON in that first step toggle their own adjacent cells. Overlapping effects can cancel.
tileturn.faq5a: Every tile must be green ✓. The cycle is dark ○ → blue ◆ → green ✓ → dark ○. A tap advances the target and its four neighbors.

colorflow.tagline: Connect matching colors, fill the grid
colorflow.metaDesc: ColorFlow is a free path-connection puzzle. Link matching color pairs and fill every cell. Over 240 levels!
colorflow.guide: Connect each pair of matching colored markers by dragging horizontally or vertically. Raised paths cannot overlap. Backtrack to shorten a path, or start again at an endpoint to redraw it. Connect every pair to complete the level; filling the entire board is an extra challenge, not a requirement to finish. Coverage gives one star below 80%, two from 80%, and three at 100%. Full coverage also doubles the score through the Flow Bonus; there is no shortest-path bonus. Follow the matching symbols as well as colors, and leave corridors for pairs farther apart. Five packs contain 150 levels on boards from 5×5 to 9×9.
colorflow.faq1q: How do I erase a path?
colorflow.faq1a: Trace backwards to shorten it, or select an endpoint to redraw that color’s path.
colorflow.faq2a: Connect every pair and cover every cell for three stars and double the total score. Shorter paths do not earn a separate bonus.
colorflow.faq3a: Five packs of 30 levels: 150 total. Boards range from 5×5 to 9×9.

pipelink.metaDesc: PipeLink is a circuit connection puzzle. Rotate tiles to connect the energy source to its destination. Features dual sources and locked tiles!
pipelink.guide: Rotate the raised circuit tiles to connect the circular energy source to the square destination with the same letter. Tap an unlocked tile for a clockwise quarter-turn; a double tap turns it halfway. Lit channels show which cells receive power. From pack 4, both A→A and B→B must connect at once. Cross tiles can carry the routes independently. Pack 5 adds locked tiles that cannot rotate. Completing the required connections wins; you do not need to power every tile. Stars depend on rotations compared with a target derived from the rotatable tile count, not a proven shortest solution. Plan before turning and use Undo to compare routes. Five packs contain 125 levels.
pipelink.faq1a: Pack 5 includes locked tiles. Their orientation is fixed, so rotate the surrounding circuit instead.
pipelink.faq2a: From pack 4, connect A→A and B→B simultaneously. Cross tiles keep the two channels independent.
pipelink.faq3q: How do levels and stars work?
pipelink.faq3a: There are 125 levels in five packs. Let N be the number of unlocked tiles excluding empty and cross tiles: at most 1.5×N rotations earns three stars, at most 2×N earns two, otherwise one. This is a scoring target, not a proven optimum.
pipelink.faq4a: Finishing without hints earns a ×1.2 multiplier. Help is currently free; if a reward ad provider is connected, it will ask before showing an ad.

mergechain.metaDesc: MergeChain is a number-merging drop game. Combine matching balls to reach 2048! Simple physics, endless strategy.
mergechain.guide: MergeChain turns number matching into a small physics puzzle. Aim the marble along the top, then release to drop it into the vessel. Two touching marbles with the same number combine into one larger marble: 2 becomes 4, then 8, 16, and beyond 2048. Bigger values take more space, so plan room for the marble that will appear after a merge. The number remains printed on each marble, making matching possible without relying on color.
mergechain.faq1a: Marbles fall, bounce, and roll against walls, the floor, and each other. Larger values have larger radii. The aiming circle shows first contact, not the final resting place.
mergechain.faq2a: A merge earns the new value multiplied by the chain. Merges within one second grow it. A fresh drop or a longer gap ends the chain.
mergechain.faq3q: What happens above the danger line?
mergechain.faq3a: Settled marbles above the danger line start a grace period: Easy gives four seconds, Normal three, Hard two and a half, and Expert two. Newly dropped marbles are excluded briefly while falling. Bring the pile down before the timer ends.
mergechain.faq4a: The marble at the top is your next drop. Easy draws 2 or 4; Normal and Hard draw 2, 4, or 8; Expert can also draw 16. Equal numbers merge into larger ones.
mergechain.faq5a: The hint suggests a column above a matching marble. The aiming guide estimates the first contact only; bouncing and rolling can change the result. Help is currently available without an ad. If a reward provider is enabled later, it will ask before showing a reward ad.
mergechain.guide2: While aiming, the dotted line and outlined circle mark the first contact along a straight drop. A green guide identifies an equal-number target. This is a planning aid, not a promise of the final resting place: moving marbles, collisions, and rolling can change the outcome. You can also focus the board, use the left and right arrow keys to aim, and press Space or Enter to drop. The short drop cooldown gives the pile time to settle.
mergechain.guide3: Each merge scores the new value, multiplied by the current chain. Quick follow-up merges grow that multiplier; a new drop or a one-second gap ends the chain. Watch the dashed danger line. Settled marbles extending above it start a grace period of two to four seconds depending on difficulty. Freshly dropped marbles have a brief exclusion while falling. Easy has slow gravity and only 2s and 4s; higher difficulties add larger drops and increase pressure over time. Daily repeats its seeded drop sequence at the selected difficulty. Time Attack gives you two minutes. A hint suggests a matching column; it does not solve the physics for you.

hexmatch.tagline: Match hex tiles in chain reactions
hexmatch.metaDesc: HexMatch is a hexagonal color matching puzzle. Connect same-colored tiles, trigger hex bombs, and survive the rising tide!
hexmatch.guide: Connect matching crystals by dragging through neighboring hexagons. A chain needs at least three crystals before you release it. Each color also carries a shape mark, so you can identify matching tiles without relying only on hue. The visible numbered line follows your selection. Its green outline and the status below the board tell you when the chain is ready and how many points releasing it will earn. You can shorten a chain by moving back to its previous crystal.
hexmatch.faq1q: How do I make a chain?
hexmatch.faq1a: Drag through at least three neighboring crystals of one color, then release. Each hex has up to six neighbors. Backtrack to the previous crystal to shorten the selection.
hexmatch.faq2a: A chain of five or more leaves a bomb near its middle. Tap it when the board is ready to clear occupied tiles within two rings, earning 20 points per destroyed tile.
hexmatch.faq3a: Every eight completed chains, columns shift upward and refill below. An occupied top cell pushed off the board ends the run. Bomb taps do not advance this chain counter.
hexmatch.faq4a: A rainbow star appears every eight completed chains and can join any one color in a chain. It does not allow mixing two different ordinary colors.
hexmatch.faq5a: 3 crystals: 30 points; 4: 60; 5: 120; 6: 300; 7 or more: 600. Five or more also creates a bomb. Explosions earn 20 points per destroyed tile.
hexmatch.faq6a: The hint outlines a numbered, traceable path of four matching crystals if possible, or three when only a shorter path is available. Follow the numbers in order. Help is currently available without an ad; a configured reward provider would ask first. If no match exists, use Shuffle.
hexmatch.guide2: Three crystals score 30 points, four score 60, five score 120, six score 300, and seven or more score 600. Chains of five or more also leave a bomb near their middle. Tap a bomb when the board is ready to clear occupied cells within two hexagon rings, scoring 20 points for each destroyed tile. Rainbow stars can join any one color in a chain. They appear every eight completed chains.
hexmatch.guide3: After a clear, tiles settle along the board's slanted columns and refill while leaving the top of each column open. Every eighth completed chain triggers Rising Tide, which shifts the columns upward and adds new tiles below. If an occupied top cell would be pushed out, the run ends. A countdown helps you prepare before the next rise. The hint button highlights a numbered path of four crystals when possible, otherwise a valid three-crystal path. Follow those numbers rather than tracing an entire connected group. If there is no match, the shuffle button rearranges colors. Continue is available once after a run ends.

pages.aboutContent: PuzzleVault is a collection of 10 free brain puzzle games that run entirely in your browser. No downloads. No accounts. No personal data collected. Just pure puzzle fun. Every game features daily challenges, score tracking, and unique mechanics you won't find anywhere else. Built with love using vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

pages.privacyNoData: We do not collect any personal data. No accounts, no sign-ups, no tracking.
pages.privacyLocalStorage: Game progress is saved locally in your browser using localStorage. This data never leaves your device.
pages.privacyAds: Google AdSense displays ads on this site and may use cookies. For details, see Google's privacy policy.
